Topics · Prayer and closeness to God

I was born Muslim and I feel nothing. Am I one?

The Quran separates saying, submitting and the heart, and this verse calls none of them a liar. 'Not yet' leaves the door open.

Part 1 of 3

﴿قَالَتِ ٱلْأَعْرَابُ ءَامَنَّا ۖ قُل لَّمْ تُؤْمِنُوا۟ وَلَـٰكِن قُولُوٓا۟ أَسْلَمْنَا وَلَمَّا يَدْخُلِ ٱلْإِيمَـٰنُ فِى قُلُوبِكُمْ ۖ وَإِن تُطِيعُوا۟ ٱللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُۥ لَا يَلِتْكُم مِّنْ أَعْمَـٰلِكُمْ شَيْـًٔا ۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ غَفُورٌ رَّحِيمٌ﴾

Translation of the meaning

The bedouins say, "We have believed." Say, "You have not [yet] believed; but say [instead], 'We have submitted,' for faith has not yet entered your hearts. And if you obey Allāh and His Messenger, He will not deprive you from your deeds[1522] of anything. Indeed, Allāh is Forgiving and Merciful."

Translator's notes

[1522] i.e., the reward thereof.

Quran · Al-Hujurat 49:14

Translation

You believe that God is one. You do well. The demons also believe—and shudder.

Original · Ancient Greek

σὺ πιστεύεις ὅτι εἷς ἐστιν ὁ θεός; καλῶς ποιεῖς· καὶ τὰ δαιμόνια πιστεύουσιν καὶ φρίσσουσιν.

James · 2:19

World English Bible

The verse names people who said: we believe. It tells them: you have not believed yet, but say we have submitted, for faith has not yet entered your hearts. Notice the word 'not yet', not 'never'. The book separates what is said, what is done, and what has entered the heart. This verse calls none of them a liar. It says the matter is not complete, and leaves the door open.

A question for you

Which is nearest to where you are?

If you sayI do what I was raised to do and feel nothing.
ThenThe verse knows this distinction between doing and the heart, and does not call it a lie.
If you sayI doubt that I believe what I say.
ThenThere is a page that looks at doubt without guilt, and it is for you.
If you sayI am afraid my family will find out.
ThenThat is understood. There is a page on this fear, and what you read here is not sent anywhere.

Part 2 of 3

﴿وَإِذْ قَالَ إِبْرَٰهِـۧمُ رَبِّ أَرِنِى كَيْفَ تُحْىِ ٱلْمَوْتَىٰ ۖ قَالَ أَوَلَمْ تُؤْمِن ۖ قَالَ بَلَىٰ وَلَـٰكِن لِّيَطْمَئِنَّ قَلْبِى ۖ قَالَ فَخُذْ أَرْبَعَةً مِّنَ ٱلطَّيْرِ فَصُرْهُنَّ إِلَيْكَ ثُمَّ ٱجْعَلْ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ جَبَلٍ مِّنْهُنَّ جُزْءًا ثُمَّ ٱدْعُهُنَّ يَأْتِينَكَ سَعْيًا ۚ وَٱعْلَمْ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ عَزِيزٌ حَكِيمٌ﴾

Translation of the meaning

And [mention] when Abraham said, "My Lord, show me how You give life to the dead." [Allāh] said, "Have you not believed?" He said, "Yes, but [I ask] only that my heart may be satisfied." [Allāh] said, "Take four birds and commit them to yourself.[107] Then [after slaughtering them] put on each hill a portion of them; then call them - they will come [flying] to you in haste. And know that Allāh is Exalted in Might and Wise."

Translator's notes

[107] i.e., train them to come to you on command.

Quran · Al-Baqarah 2:260

Translation

As it is written, “I have made you a father of many nations.” This is in the presence of him whom he believed: God, who gives life to the dead, and calls the things that are not, as though they were. Against hope, Abraham in hope believed, to the end that he might become a father of many nations, according to that which had been spoken, “So will your offspring be.” Without being weakened in faith, he didn’t consider his own body, already having been worn out, (he being about a hundred years old), and the deadness of Sarah’s womb. Yet, looking to the promise of God, he didn’t waver through unbelief, but grew strong through faith, giving glory to God, and being fully assured that what he had promised, he was also able to perform.

Original · Ancient Greek

καθὼς γέγραπται ὅτι Πατέρα πολλῶν ἐθνῶν τέθεικά σε), κατέναντι οὗ ἐπίστευσεν θεοῦ τοῦ ζῳοποιοῦντος τοὺς νεκροὺς καὶ καλοῦντος τὰ μὴ ὄντα ὡς ὄντα· ὃς παρʼ ἐλπίδα ἐπʼ ἐλπίδι ἐπίστευσεν εἰς τὸ γενέσθαι αὐτὸν πατέρα πολλῶν ἐθνῶν κατὰ τὸ εἰρημένον· Οὕτως ἔσται τὸ σπέρμα σου· καὶ μὴ ἀσθενήσας τῇ πίστει κατενόησεν τὸ ἑαυτοῦ σῶμα νενεκρωμένον, ἑκατονταετής που ὑπάρχων, καὶ τὴν νέκρωσιν τῆς μήτρας Σάρρας, εἰς δὲ τὴν ἐπαγγελίαν τοῦ θεοῦ οὐ διεκρίθη τῇ ἀπιστίᾳ ἀλλὰ ἐνεδυναμώθη τῇ πίστει, δοὺς δόξαν τῷ θεῷ καὶ πληροφορηθεὶς ὅτι ὃ ἐπήγγελται δυνατός ἐστιν καὶ ποιῆσαι.

Romans · 4:17-21

World English Bible

In the Quran Abraham says: my Lord, show me how You give life to the dead. God asks: do you not believe? He answers: yes, but so that my heart may be at rest. He believes, and still wants his heart to settle. The text neither refuses the request nor scolds him for it. It answers him. Belief and rest are two things in the sentence, and the second can be asked for and given.

A question for you

What do you take from Abraham's answer?

If you sayThat asking for rest is allowed.
ThenThe verse says so. It does not call it weakness.
If you sayThat the two are not one thing.
ThenYes, and that leaves wide room for someone who wants to proceed quietly.
If you sayI do not know what my heart needs.
ThenThat too is an honest place to begin. The next step tells you where you are waited for.

Part 3 of 3

﴿وَإِذَا سَأَلَكَ عِبَادِى عَنِّى فَإِنِّى قَرِيبٌ ۖ أُجِيبُ دَعْوَةَ ٱلدَّاعِ إِذَا دَعَانِ ۖ فَلْيَسْتَجِيبُوا۟ لِى وَلْيُؤْمِنُوا۟ بِى لَعَلَّهُمْ يَرْشُدُونَ﴾

Translation of the meaning

And when My servants ask you, [O Muḥammad], concerning Me - indeed I am near. I respond to the invocation of the supplicant when he calls upon Me. So let them respond to Me [by obedience] and believe in Me that they may be [rightly] guided.

Quran · Al-Baqarah 2:186

Translation

Yahweh is near to all those who call on him, to all who call on him in truth.

Original · Hebrew

קָר֣וֹב יְ֭הוָה לְכָל־קֹרְאָ֑יו לְכֹ֤ל אֲשֶׁ֖ר יִקְרָאֻ֣הוּ בֶאֱמֶֽת׃

the Psalms · 145:18

World English Bible

The verse says God is near and answers the call of the one who calls. It adds: so let them respond to Me and believe in Me, that they may be rightly guided. The first sentence is about what God does, the second an invitation to respond. Neither sets a precondition on what the heart feels. Rest is not a condition of calling; calling may be its road.

A question for you

Which step seems possible to you?

If you sayOne honest sentence.
ThenBegin with it. That is all the verse asks at the start.
If you sayTo read and ask.
ThenThat is another road, and reflection has a place here.
If you sayTo wait a little.
ThenWaiting is allowed. It does not close the door.

The same in the other books
